title: N45 ITFlow Goals 1-5 acceptance map
evidence_policy: Synthetic and local evidence verifies behavior only. Production evidence remains pending or externally recorded and is never promoted by this manifest.

requirements.text: One canonical ITFlow device record exists for each managed endpoint.

production_evidence.needed: Export active managed assets after replay and a scheduled reconciliation cycle and prove one canonical asset per endpoint.

requirements.text: Every connected system uses a durable external identity mapping.

production_evidence.needed: Verify every required production source mapping has its immutable source object ID and approved tenant/site scope.

requirements.text: Each device exposes a source coverage matrix with status and last-seen timestamps.
Client reconciliation exposes missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting and orphaned records.
Ambiguous matches become safe review suggestions.
Source ingestion is idempotent under replay.
Automated and manual mapping decisions retain an audit trail.
Every active managed endpoint has one canonical ITFlow asset.

production_evidence.needed: Run the read-only burn-in export against production after replay and at least one scheduled cycle.

requirements.text: Each required inventory source is mapped by immutable external identifier.

production_evidence.needed: Review the production per-asset required-source policy and prove exact source coverage.

requirements.text: Replaying a device payload creates no new asset or mapping.
Automation cannot silently move a device between clients.
Missing Level, SentinelOne or Intune coverage is visible without opening source consoles.
Hostname changes and rebuilds preserve historical identity integrity.
Conflicts and ambiguous matches enter a review queue.
Mapping decisions and overrides are auditable.
Tests cover matching, duplicates, tenant conflicts, stale records and retirement.
Events use fingerprint-based deduplication.
Incidents retain repeat counters and first/last occurrence timestamps.
Recovery updates or resolves the existing ticket.
Maintenance windows suppress noise without erasing history.
Ticket creation thresholds are configurable.
Failures support retry, dead-letter review and replay.
Retained raw payloads are secret-redacted.
Incidents link directly to client, device, service and ticket.
Every supported source can produce the canonical event contract.

production_evidence.reference: Enhancement goals Goal 2 delivery slices 2E and change log.

requirements.text: Repeated delivery cannot repeat ticket side effects.
Semantic repeats increment counters without ticket noise.
Maintenance and threshold suppression are visible and auditable.
Recovery updates or resolves the correct existing ticket.

production_evidence.reference: Enhancement goals Goal 2 representative source production matrix.

requirements.text: Transient failures retry and terminal failures can be replayed.
Retained payloads contain no source credentials or secret values.
Actionable incidents link to the correct operational objects.
CI, migration and production canary validation complete.

production_evidence.reference: Enhancement goals Goal 2 delivery slice 2F; not re-certified by local audit.

requirements.text: Each execution is pinned to one ticket, client, project context, published version, snapshot and hash.
Task state is explicit: Ready, Blocked, Waiting, Completed or Skipped.
Dependencies, conditions, owners, approvals, due offsets and evidence rules validate and enforce.
Every ticket lifecycle surface uses transactional workflow gates.
Requesters cannot self-approve and guest credentials are hashed, bounded and one-use.
Task-state and approval histories are append-only.
Evidence files and rows commit or clean up together and referenced attachments cannot be deleted.
The client-safe closeout validates immutable definition, runtime state, evidence and histories.
Published versions and execution snapshots cannot be rewritten by draft edits.
Task workflow metadata and transitions enforce transactionally.
Every ticket lifecycle surface fails closed with unfinished workflow work.
Approval credentials cannot be recovered from storage, exports, logs or history.
Approval and state histories reconstruct every terminal task.
Evidence cannot be orphaned by rollback or removed while referenced.
Canonical onboarding and offboarding definitions reconcile deterministically.
A completed execution produces an integrity-checked client-safe closeout.
CI, migration, reconciliation and production onboarding/offboarding canaries complete.

production_evidence.needed: After deployment, complete one synthetic-client onboarding and one offboarding through the authenticated integrity-verified closeout export.

requirements.text: Applicability derives deterministically from active plan, services, assets and integration coverage.
An unrelated similarly named file cannot make a missing requirement current.
Verification requires an authorized actor or trusted automation and records evidence.
Review dates derive from verified timestamp and published cadence.
Exceptions require reason, distinct approver, expiry and audit history.
Configuration-changing tickets link affected documentation obligations.
Resolution blocks on missing or stale affected documentation absent valid exception or waiver.
Readiness uses the same evaluated obligation rows shown to technicians.
Re-evaluation is idempotent and preserves verification history.
Every managed client has a deterministic required documentation set.
Every obligation has owner, status, verification source, cadence and explainable freshness.
Missing, due-soon, stale and expiring-exception work is visible centrally.
Configuration-changing tickets cannot close with unresolved affected documentation.
Exceptions and waivers expire, are auditable and do not rewrite base freshness.
Readiness is reproducible from technician-visible obligation rows.
Evidence Locker, Change Passport and Promise Ledger updates are transactional and traceable.
Re-evaluation is idempotent and preserves verification decisions.
CI, migration, reconciliation and all five production scenarios complete.

production_evidence.needed: After deployment, complete honest current, stale, missing, exception and closure-gate canaries using a second authorized exception approver without backdating evidence.

requirements.text: The unified record includes assigned user and Entra/Intune identity.
The unified record includes compliance, encryption, Secure Boot, OS and build.
The unified record includes Level and SentinelOne health.
The unified record includes warranty and lifecycle state.
The unified record includes physical and virtual interfaces.
The unified record retains MAC and IP history.
The unified record retains VLAN, switch-port and LLDP/CDP relationships.
The unified record includes a device and network change timeline.
The unified record links related tickets, changes, evidence and documentation.
The consolidated editable Network Interfaces view and collapsed read-only observations are deployed together.

production_evidence.needed: Deploy the combined release candidate and run the asset Network Interfaces presentation canary on production.
